newsitem.title: USA: First Merchants Q4 loan loss provision up.
newsitem.headline: First Merchants Q4 loan loss provision up.

text.p: First Merchants Acceptance Corp said Tuesday its loan loss provision for the fourth quarter jumped, due to implementation of a new credit scoring system.
The provision in the fourth quarter was $9.9 million, up from $1.1 million a year ago, the used car finance company said.
Also, net charge-offs as a percentage of average net finance receivables serviced were 6.8 percent for the year, compared to 5.2 percent for the prior year period, the company said.

"While our delinquency is still below that of our peers, by using these new analytical tools, we concluded in early December that charge-offs would likely increase in the short term, so we have added to our loss reserves," Mitchell Kahn, president and chief executive officer, said in a news release.
He added that the company expects the charge-off rate in the first half of 1997 will be higher than the levels experienced in the corresponding 1996 periods due to normal aging of the portfolio.
"We do not expect the charge-off rate to increase significantly from the fourth quarter," he said. "More importantly, we have strengthened our loss reserves and collection procedures."
Earlier Tuesday, the company reported net income of $1 million, or $0.15 a share for the fourth quarter, compared to $2.5 million, or $0.38 a share a year ago.
The decline in net income was due to higher-than anticipated charge-offs and addtions to loan loss reserves, First Merchants said.
The stock closed down 1-3/4 at 13-3/8 Tuesday.
